verified: The Decoder reported on 25 November 2026 that US chip-access curbs, anti-distillation measures and reduced access to Nvidia hardware abroad are pressuring DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba, and that DeepSeek researchers have internally estimated a gap of up to nine months behind US models — claims the outlet attributes to a report it does not name.
unconfirmed: The nine-month figure, the assertion that the gap is widening, and the causal link to export controls and anti-distillation rules all rest on that single unnamed report; no methodology, measurement basis or independent benchmark is given, none of the three labs has commented on the record, and the report is not identified so it cannot be checked.

verified: The Decoder 报道称，据一份报告，美国的芯片出口限制、反蒸馏措施以及海外获取英伟达硬件渠道的收窄，正给 DeepSeek、Moonshot AI 和阿里巴巴带来压力。外部资料显示，DeepSeek 早前曾使用为符合美国出口管制而设计的降规版英伟达 H800 芯片训练模型（WIRED 报道）。
unconfirmed: DeepSeek 研究人员“内部估计落后美国模型至多九个月”且差距正在扩大这一说法，仅来自该报道转述的一份未具名、未链接的报告，没有 DeepSeek 或任何实验室的公开确认，也无独立测量佐证；反蒸馏措施具体如何拖慢研发、三家实验室各自受到多大影响，以及该估算的基准模型与时间点，报道均未说明。

titles.en: Report says US chip curbs are slowing DeepSeek, Moonshot and Alibaba
titles.zh: 报道称美国芯片管制与反蒸馏措施已拖慢中国AI实验室
